text: Telescopes and nebulae are fundamental tools for astronomers. These instruments allow us to gather light from small mirrors, which in turn helps us to understand the cosmos. Nebulae, vast clouds of gas and dust, are particularly crucial as they only become visible when a telescope is pointed towards them. The study of these cosmic phenomena is a key part of the astronomical narrative, with the telescope and nebula serving as the starting points for many observations. Telescopes are mechanical devices that produce light from small mirrors, while nebulae are clouds of gas and dust that surround the stars, becoming visible only when their path is revealed by the telescope.
